blocks.text: Why Movavi video editor problems happen on Mac

Software maintenance is an invisible tax on your creative time. Video editing software is not a static tool. It relies on a complex stack of OS updates, GPU drivers, and third-party plugins. When one part of your Mac updates, others may break. This creates a chain reaction of errors.

Tool sprawl is another major culprit. You likely juggle multiple apps for audio, grading, and motion graphics. Each requires its own cache management. When you switch between these apps, your system memory can become fragmented. This leads to the classic 'Not Responding' error in Movavi.
Routine maintenance fixes for your workflow

items: Clear media cache: Go to your editor preferences and locate the cache folder. Delete old files to free up space and resolve playback stutters.
Use proxy files: If you edit 4K footage, create low-resolution proxy files first. This reduces the load on your hardware and prevents crashes during the editing process.
Manage background tasks: Open Activity Monitor by pressing ⌘ + Space, then typing 'Activity Monitor'. Check the CPU tab to see if other apps are hogging resources while you edit.
Check for updates manually: Instead of relying on auto-updates, check the developer website for stable versions before updating your OS.

blocks.text: Your Mac is a professional tool. Treat it like one. If you install many plugins, some may conflict with your editing software. Use App Cleaner & Uninstaller to ensure no leftover files remain after you remove an app. These stray files are frequent causes of system instability.
Before you update your Mac, create a full backup using Time Machine. If a new update breaks your workflow, you can restore your previous stable environment.

faq.question: Why does my video editor crash when I export?
faq.answer: Export crashes are often caused by full storage or corrupted cache files. Clear your cache and ensure you have at least 20% of your disk space free.

faq.question: Should I update my Mac OS while working on a project?
faq.answer: No. Never update your operating system or editing software in the middle of a project. Professionals wait until the project is finished to avoid compatibility issues.
